fee.collection: accrued in the vault outside the backing; anyone calls sweepFees() and the vault pays the recipient
fee.networkFee: the depositor pays the deposit transaction (about 115,000 energy on a private TVM, before USDT's dynamic-energy penalty, plus an approval); the relayer pays the release transaction (about 143,000 energy before the penalty)

finality.rule: A deposit is attested only when the signer's own java-tron node serves it from the solidified state (/walletsolidity): its block has been confirmed by more than 70% of the 27 block producers (19).
finality.reorg: Signers never read the head for a deposit, so a deposit that leaves the head chain before solidification is never attested. Solidified blocks do not revert while fewer than a third of the block producers are faulty. If a solidified deposit vanished anyway, its mint is still inside the 12 hour L2 delay: 2 of the 3 guardians cancel it on the L2 (or pause the L2 token when they cannot), so it is never credited. The vault itself is paused by a guardian on a reserves shortfall or on evidence of a forged mint, not on a missing deposit alone. A mint that did credit holds later releases instead of paying them (the vault pays only burns made under its own deposit chain).

deposit.recipientEncoding: bytes32: the 20-byte L2 address left-padded with zeros
steps: approve the vault for the amount on the USDT contract (TRC-20 approve)
call deposit(amount, l2Recipient) on the vault
after the block is solidified (about a minute) and the 12 hour mint delay the L2 token credits amount less 0.05% to l2Recipient
refusals: an amount below minDeposit or above maxDeposit, or one that would pass the cap
an l2Recipient that is zero or longer than 20 bytes
do not name a contract as l2Recipient unless it can move the token
a deposit while the issuer has blacklisted the vault or replaced (deprecated) the token: the vault refuses it (TokenUnsafe)
a deposit while the token is paused or charges a transfer fee: the transaction reverts

release.recipientEncoding: the 20-byte form of the TRON address: Base58Check-decode the T... address, check its checksum, drop the leading 0x41 byte
notes: USDT on TRON pays a recipient the issuer has blacklisted (the funds are then frozen at that address by the issuer, not by the bridge)
while the issuer has blacklisted the vault, paused the token or switched a transfer fee on, no release can be paid; burns stay payable and are paid when the condition ends
the recipient needs no TRX and no activated account to receive USDT
UNAUDITED. Nothing is deployed. Limits are the Ethereum bridge's launch values, proposed for this network; the owner confirms them before deployment.

TRON addresses: custody.address, asset.id and fee.recipient are Base58Check (T...). committee addresses are the 20-byte 0x form of the same keys; the T... form of a key is Base58Check(0x41 || those 20 bytes).
The L2 token's sourceChainId is 728126428 and its sourceVault is the vault's 20-byte address.
